He also talks about how he could kick anyone's ass and how he's still in great shape, even though he's a bit older and not as fit as he used to be. I know for a fact that most of this is just bull because when I tried to look him up online, there was nothing about him being a professional boxer. That makes me think he's lying to make himself seem better than he actually is. On the other hand, I'm 19 and have been training in Muay Thai for eight years. I also wrestled in high school, so I'm pretty confident in my own skills and physical fitness. I take pride in my progress in martial arts and fitness, especially since I used to be overweight and out of shape. I rarely hang out with Jackson outside of work because he never stops talking about his supposed achievements and other lies, like getting kicked out of culinary school for fighting or knowing high-profile gangbangers who make millions a year. He claims he works at the restaurant just for fun, not because he needs the money. But last weekend, we ended up hanging out, having a few beers, and watching UFC. During the Blagoy Ivanov vs. Taimur Islamov fight, Jackson said, "I could KO both these bums, no challenge." That's when I snapped and told him I doubted he could even kick my ass, especially since I'm 19 and half his weight. I also called him out on his boxing lies and mentioned that nothing shows up when you Google his name. I challenged him to come down to my Muay Thai gym and try, saying I'd "maul" him. He got all pissy and walked out, and then I told some of the coworkers I liked about it. Now, most of my coworkers think I'm a asshole for calling him out like that, although a few agreed with me. Let me think about the different aspects of this situation. First, there's the issue of honesty and integrity. I believe in being truthful, and I was frustrated with Jackson constantly lying about his achievements. By calling him out, I was standing up for what I think is right. However, I also need to consider how I went about doing it. Did I handle the situation in a mature and respectful way? I snapped at him during a casual hangout, which might not have been the best approach. Maybe there's a more constructive way to address his lies without confronting him publicly or in a heated manner. Also, by telling other coworkers about it, I might have contributed to a negative work environment or made things awkward between us. Another thing to consider is the power dynamic between us. Jackson is older and has been working there longer, so he might feel entitled to his position or reputation. By challenging him, I might have threatened his ego or sense of self, leading to tension in the workplace. Additionally, I need to reflect on my own motivations. Was I calling him out because I truly believed he was lying and wanted to set the record straight, or was there an element of personal pride or jealousy involved? It's important to examine my intentions to ensure that my actions were driven by a desire for honesty rather than a need to assert my own superiority. Moreover, I should think about the potential consequences of my actions. Jackson walked out after I confronted him, and now most coworkers think I'm a asshole. This could affect our working relationship and create an uncomfortable atmosphere. It might also make it harder for me to be taken seriously in the future if I'm seen as confrontational or disrespectful. On the positive side, a few coworkers agreed with me, which suggests that some people appreciate honesty and integrity. However, the majority's negative reaction indicates that my approach might have been off. Perhaps there's a better way to address the issue without causing conflict. In summary, while I believe in standing up for honesty and integrity, I need to evaluate whether calling out Jackson in the way I did was the most effective and respectful approach. It might have been justified in terms of the content, but the manner in which I did it could be seen as wrong or unwise, especially considering the negative reactions from most coworkers and the potential for workplace tension. I should also consider seeking advice from a trusted mentor or counselor to gain a different perspective and learn healthier ways to handle such situations in the future. It's important to balance my values with the practical aspects of maintaining positive relationships and a harmonious work environment.
